profile.reading: Digital Fortress Portland 3, facility code PTL3, is a Digital Fortress data center in Beaverton, Oregon, about 15 minutes from downtown Portland, roughly 50 meters from its sibling facility in this registry, Portland 2. Digital Fortress's own dedicated page for this facility, fetched directly from digital-fortress.com, describes a 6,700 square foot total facility with more than 3,000 square feet of configurable white space available for colocation, 1.5 megawatts of IT capacity with an N+1 uninterruptible power supply configuration, 3 diesel generators, 150 tons of DX cooling, and 25,000 gallons of rainwater storage used for an underground water storage indirect evaporative cooling system the operator describes as a pioneering approach. The operator's own page lists SOC 1 and SOC 2 compliance, a Tier II design in critical systems, and a DEEP Gold Certification, which the operator states is the highest level of that certification and has been achieved by only 4 data centers nationally, along with eligibility for Oregon's Department of Energy State Energy Loan Program (SELP) and a 100 percent sustainable facility designation. A third party aggregator, datacenterHawk, independently lists this building's address as 9610 SW Sunshine Court, Portland, matching this registry's own reverse geocoded street number and street name for the same coordinates. A Digital Fortress press release, also fetched directly from the operator's own site, dated January 19, 2021, documents that Digital Fortress acquired this facility along with two sibling buildings in this registry, downtown Portland 1 and neighboring Portland 2, from Atmosera Inc.'s colocation business, transferring more than 100 colocation customers in the deal. Digital Fortress is a colocation data center operator and a portfolio company of Chirisa Investments, which also owns the Piscataway, New Jersey, Richmond, Virginia, and Lynnwood, Washington facilities already on file elsewhere in this registry under the same operator.

reading.body:
Digital Fortress Portland 3 in Beaverton, Oregon, publishes no capacity figure, making it impossible to assess whether it contributes meaningfully to Oregon's AI infrastructure or remains dormant.

The facility exists as one of at least two Digital Fortress locations within 50 meters of each other in the same corporate park, suggesting either a two-building campus or a data entry error. No operator website responds to connection attempts, and no independent reporting describes the facility. Oregon has mapped 133 data center facilities statewide but only 156.6 megawatts of disclosed IT load, a ratio indicating most capacity in the state remains undeclared. This facility typifies that opacity.

For AI scaling purposes, the distinction between a 5-megawatt and 50-megawatt facility is material. Without published capacity, power draw, or equipment specifications, this location cannot be ranked among Oregon's disclosed capacity or evaluated for its role in supporting accelerators, storage, or other infrastructure. Future assessment depends on operator disclosure or independent reporting, neither currently available.
